questions.stem: A nightly production job must start quickly with no cluster to configure, and the team wants to pay only while it runs. Which compute fits best?

options.text: Serverless compute for jobs
A SQL warehouse for the Python job
A personal laptop
An all-purpose cluster left running

questions.explanation: Serverless compute is managed by Databricks, so there's no cluster to configure, and it minimizes idle time.

questions.stem: Analysts run SQL queries and dashboards against gold tables. Which compute is designed for that?

options.text: A Lakeflow Connect gateway
A job cluster
A SQL warehouse
A single-node all-purpose cluster with ML runtime

questions.explanation: SQL warehouses are compute built for SQL queries, dashboards and BI tools.

questions.stem: What does auto termination do on an all-purpose compute resource?

options.text: Terminates the compute after it has been idle for the time you set
Moves its jobs to a SQL warehouse
Restarts it every hour
Deletes the notebooks attached to it

questions.explanation: With auto termination, Databricks terminates compute that has been inactive for the set number of minutes, so it doesn't run up cost.

questions.stem: Several engineers want one classic compute resource they can share, to collaborate at low cost. Which type fits?

options.text: A Lakeflow Connect gateway
A SQL warehouse for their Python code
Standard (multi-user) compute
No compute; notebooks run in the browser

questions.explanation: Standard compute is multi-user compute with shared resources for cost-effective collaboration.

questions.stem: Which two are characteristics of serverless compute? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: It can't run notebooks
It always runs the latest runtime version
You must install the runtime by hand
You choose every VM type yourself
Databricks allocates and manages the compute resources

questions.explanation: With serverless, Databricks automatically allocates and manages the compute, and workloads run on the latest runtime version.
